what: The id-registration script used Path.write_text on tests/orchestration/expected.json. On Windows that translates every LF to CRLF, so a 1-line append rewrote all 117 lines of a file shared with the accepted W06 increment-2 work and with ops/ci/orchestration.py.
detected_by: git show --stat on commit 94f2126b reported 233 changed lines for a file where 2 were intended; a byte check showed old CRLF=0 LF=116 versus new CRLF=117 LF=0.

impact_assessed.test_semantics: unchanged - JSON content identical apart from the intended 12-id entry; ids are compared as sets at ops/ci/orchestration.py:109

recovery: rebuilt from the git show HEAD~1 blob bytes, same targeted replace with count asserts, written with write_bytes so no EOL translation occurs
re-ran the full W06-G01 name list against the restored bytes instead of assuming the earlier result holds
rule: Hash-frozen evidence is never rewritten and a committed artifact is never silently reworded; corrections land in a new file. Future shared-file edits in this repo must use write_bytes or open(newline=...) plus a diff-size assert.
